response: The year in which radical prostatectomy (RP) was performed is indeed a predictor of outcome in prostate cancer. When controlling for preoperative features, the year of RP has been shown to be a significant predictor of outcome on multivariate analysis, and this effect cannot be explained by stage migration. This suggests that advancements in surgical techniques, technology, or postoperative care over time may contribute to improved outcomes for patients undergoing radical prostatectomy.
